title: Decode String
corePattern: Stack for Nested Structures and Recursion for Bracket Matching
interviewTips: Ask if k can have multiple digits like 100[ab] and if nesting can be deep, to confirm you need curNum = curNum*10 + digit.
Trade-off: two-stack iterative avoids recursion depth limits and is easy to trace, recursion with shared index is cleaner but uses call stack O(depth).
Edge-case tip: always reset curNum after '[' and handle plain letters outside brackets like 2[abc]3[cd]ef.

approaches.name: Approach 1: Two Stacks Iterative
approaches.intuition: Brackets are LIFO: when we see '[' we save what we have built so far and the repeat count, then start fresh inside. When we see ']' we pop and expand.
approaches.theory: Maintain numStack for k and strStack for previous built string. curNum accumulates multi-digit numbers. curStr accumulates current level characters. On '[' push state and reset. On ']' pop repeat r and prev, set curStr = prev + curStr*r. Each character processed once, stack depth equals nesting depth.

timeComplexity.explanation: N is length of decoded output plus input scan. Each input char processed once, each output char built once via repetition. In worst case repeated copying dominates but amortized linear in output size.

spaceComplexity.explanation: D is nesting depth for two stacks, N is decoded output length stored in curStr and stack strings.

steps: curStr='a', curNum=2, see '[': push 2 and 'a': reset

edgeCases: Single letters without brackets: abc returns abc
Deep nesting: 3[a2[b2[c]]] stack depth grows correctly
Trailing letters: 2[abc]3[cd]ef appends ef after stacks empty

approaches.name: Approach 2: Recursion with Shared Index
approaches.intuition: Encoded string is a recursive grammar: expr := letters + k[expr]. Parse with a pointer; on '[' recurse to decode inner, on ']' return to caller.
approaches.theory: Use global index i over s. dfs() builds res for current level: accumulate num for digits, on '[' advance i and call dfs() for inner, append inner*num, on ']' advance i and return res to parent, else append letter. Recursion depth equals bracket nesting depth, naturally matching structure.

timeComplexity.explanation: Each character in s visited once via idx pointer, output built by repeating inner strings. Total time linear in decoded length.

spaceComplexity.explanation: D is max nesting depth for recursion call stack, N is output string size. No explicit stacks needed.

edgeCases: No brackets: abcd returns directly without recursion
Nested empty-like: 2[3[a]b] inner returns aaab then outer repeats
Adjacent blocks: 2[ab]3[cd] handled sequentially in same dfs level
